Thanks Sarah — great questions. Below is the recommended shortlist and the high-level rationale for each, followed by links/attachments to the benchmark results, prompt-set, and suggested rollout guardrails.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):

1) redwood/optima-7B (quantized, v2)
- Rationale: Best cost/latency balance for high-throughput production. On Redwood Hosted with our GPU autoscaling profile we see 95th-pct latency ~180–220 ms for 512-token requests; on Dedicated (p3/rtx-class) expect ~140–180 ms.
- Quality: Comparable to larger 13B models on instruction-following tasks after our prompt templates and small-context calibration.
- Cost: Lowest unit cost (approx ~$0.0009–0.002016 per 1k tokens depending on batch/caching).
- When to pick: If your priority is cost and predictable throughput for high volume workflows.

2) community/lg-13B-rlhf (float16)
- Rationale: Higher base quality on nuanced conversation and summarization tasks; higher latency & cost.
- Latency: 95th-pct ~350–420 ms hosted; ~260–320 ms on Dedicated.
- Cost: ~$0.0025–0.00235 per 1k tokens.
- When to pick: If acceptance rate based on quality metric is critical and you can tolerate higher cost/latency.

3) redwood/fast-3B (optimized-llm) — canary candidate
- Rationale: Ultra-low latency for interactive UX. Lower quality on edge cases, but excellent for short-response scenarios (quick suggestions).
- Latency: ~100–140 ms 95th-pct on Dedicated.
- Cost: ~$0.0006 per 1k tokens.
- When to pick: If interactive suggestion latency is the top priority; recommend using in a blended policy (e.g., 80% fast-3B + 20% optima-7B for higher-confidence cases).

Model evaluation artifacts included:
- Full benchmark PDF with token-cost breakdowns, latency percentiles, and eval set results (attached).
- Prompt set CSV with ~120 representative prompts covering summarization, extractive QA, contradiction/hallucination checks (attached).
- Quick-run harness: instructions to run the evals in your environment + Redwood-run results in the Drive link below.

Suggested rollout / regression guardrails:
- Canary: start at 5% traffic for 24–48 hours, monitor acceptance rate (rolling 12h) and failure/error rate.
- Automatic rollback: if acceptance rate drops >5 percentage points vs baseline OR if latency SLO breaches for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows, auto-fallback to previous model.
- A/B: run 10–30% holdout for two weeks to validate downstream metric impact (CSAT or acceptance rate).
- Monitoring: instrument token-level cost, per-route 95th pct latency, and per-prompt acceptance. Redwood Console dashboards & alerting can be pre-configured (we can share the dashboard JSON if helpful).

Security/compliance (short answers for RFP):
- SOC2: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II; PDF excerpt attached (see sla-summary.pdf).
- Data handling: default is encrypted-in-transit and at-rest; option to disable logging for sensitive routes in Dedicated.
- KMS/HSM: available for Private deployments — details in attached SLA doc.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today: I've attached the benchmark summary and prompt set. (See attached files and Drive link.)
- Tue 7/28 10:30–11:30 PT: Proposed model fit call (David + Neha) — please confirm.
- By Fri 7/31: your team runs the prompt set; share initial pass and we'll review mismatches.
